findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve AC5 into a measurable decision: either state the structural guard as a required deliverable with its observable outcome and proving check, or explicitly mark it out-of-scope / deferred to a named follow-up with rationale.
evidence: 'Consider a structural guard: a check that FAILS when a step in the Verified lane runs a repo script without the if-present guard'
'Consider' is effort/deliberation-framed, not an observable end-state; the other four ACs state concrete outcomes ('carries the ee2a guard', 'exits 0 without an ::error::')
findings.finding: Acceptance criterion 5 ('Consider a structural guard...') is framed as deliberation ('Consider') rather than a specific observable outcome, so it is ambiguous whether the structural guard is a required deliverable of this ticket or an optional suggestion, and it is not measurable as written.
scenarios: An executor reads AC5 and cannot tell whether shipping without the structural guard leaves the ticket incomplete.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to a decision, e.g. 'A structural check FAILS when a Verified-lane step runs a repo script without the ee2a if-present guard (proven by a fixture step lacking the guard)' — or 'Structural guard deferred to <ticket> because <reason>'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly why `test.yml`'s `golden-path` job (branch-head checkout, no definition-vs-tree skew) is out of scope, so the deliberate asymmetry with the guarded `gerrit-verify.yaml` golden-path is documented rather than left for the next reader to re-derive.
evidence: test.yml:104-128 defines a `golden-path` job running `python scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py` (line 126) and `python scripts/probe_rebar.py` (line 128) with plain `actions/checkout@v7` (line 108) — branch-head, no refspec
Plan quote: 'The older ones are the same latent class and should be guarded for uniformity, so the next reader does not have to re-derive which are safe.'
test.yml:16-19 states this file is the branch-head lane; branch CI runs definition and tree from the same ref, so no skew — the exclusion is correct but unstated
findings.finding: The sweep names only `_build-and-test.yml` and `gerrit-verify.yaml`, but a THIRD workflow — `test.yml:104-128` `golden-path` — runs the same `scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py` and `scripts/probe_rebar.py` unguarded. That job checks out branch-head (no Gerrit refspec), so the definition-vs-tree skew genuinely does NOT apply there and excluding it is defensible; but the plan is silent on the boundary, which undercuts its own stated 'so the next reader does not have to re-derive which are safe' rationale — a reader diffing the two near-identical golden-path jobs will find one guarded and one not.
findings.location: Plan section 'gerrit-verify.yaml's golden-path job also checks out the Gerrit patchset...' / test.yml:104-128
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the gerrit-verify.yaml paragraph noting that `test.yml`'s golden-path is the same script set but runs on branch-head (definition and tree from one ref), so it has no skew and is intentionally not guarded — and if the AC5 structural guard is built, scope it to the Verified/patchset-checkout lane so it does not flag the branch-head golden-path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Before building the AC5 structural guard, screen the existing workflow-parsing checks (scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py, tests/unit/test_git_floor_gate_tree_skew.py, scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py Layer W) and state whether the guard extends one of them or genuinely needs a new mechanism.
evidence: The repo already parses workflow YAML and enumerates steps in several checks: scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py + tests/unit/test_verify_gate_parity.py (walks vote.needs vs gating jobs), tests/unit/test_git_floor_gate_tree_skew.py (`_gate_script()` lifts a step's run: body from `workflow['jobs'].values()` → `job.get('steps', [])`), scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py 'Layer W' (workflow + shell step scanning per test_raw_git_write_lint.py), and test_ci_actionlint_scope.py.

AC5 leaves the guard's FORM unspecified (new script? new test? extend an existing parity check?), so an implementer could write a fresh YAML walker that duplicates the step-enumeration already present in check_verify_gate_parity.py / the ee2a mirrored test.
AC5 is phrased 'Consider ...' — already appropriately optional/YAGNI-conscious; this is a scoping nudge, not a demand to build it.
findings.finding: The proposed AC5 structural guard does not screen the existing family of workflow-YAML-parsing parity/lint checks as a host, risking a bespoke rebuild of step-enumeration infrastructure that already exists.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC5 ('Consider a structural guard: a check that FAILS when a step in the Verified lane runs a repo script without the if-present guard')
scenarios: Implementer builds AC5 as a standalone new scanner and re-implements workflow-step parsing that check_verify_gate_parity.py and the ee2a mirrored test already perform.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate tests/unit/test_probe_wired_into_ci.py as a consumer whose golden-path substring assertion must still hold after the guard, and note that test.yml's own golden-path job is intentionally out of scope (branch-head checkout => no definition-vs-tree skew).
evidence: tests/unit/test_probe_wired_into_ci.py parses BOTH `test.yml` and `gerrit-verify.yaml`, locates each `golden-path` job, and asserts a step's `run` text contains `scripts/probe_rebar.py` (_PROBE_JOBS = {"test.yml": "golden-path", "gerrit-verify.yaml": "golden-path"}).

.github/workflows/test.yml lines 104-128 define a SECOND `golden-path` job running `python scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py` and `python scripts/probe_rebar.py </dev/null` — the plan names only gerrit-verify.yaml's golden-path.

An if-present guard wraps the `python scripts/probe_rebar.py` call but keeps the `scripts/probe_rebar.py` substring in the step `run`, so the assertion survives — the consumer is unaffected but is a directly-asserting consumer outside the artifact the plan should confirm.
findings.finding: The plan does not enumerate tests/unit/test_probe_wired_into_ci.py as a consumer that directly asserts on the golden-path job it edits, nor does it mention test.yml's own golden-path job which runs the same two scripts.
scenarios: A reviewer or implementer re-checking the probe-wiring invariant after editing gerrit-verify.yaml's golden-path steps.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] For the AC5 structural guard, specify that it must itself carry the ee2a if-present guard (or run only in the Verified/patchset lane and skip when its own checker/target is absent), so the guard does not become its own bootstrap false-failure.
evidence: AC5: 'a check that FAILS when a step in the Verified lane runs a repo script without the if-present guard'
The ee2a note (_build-and-test.yml:138-144) is the general rule for ANY new gate step that runs a repo script — a structural-guard step is itself such a step
This is the same recursion the parent bug 7e90 hit: a gate added on main failing changes whose base predates it
findings.finding: AC5's proposed structural guard would itself be a repo script that runs in the Verified lane, making it subject to the exact definition-vs-tree skew it is meant to police (a change whose base predates the checker, or a tree lacking the checker, would either trip it or run a checker that isn't there). The plan does not address how the structural guard avoids being its own first false-failure / bootstrap case.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, item 5 ('Consider a structural guard...')
